editor_note: The meaning is faithful overall. In [10], "to more tightly bound the sensitivity to errors" becomes "mengehadkan kepekaan terhadap ralat ... dengan lebih ketat". That can be read as "restrict/reduce the sensitivity", when the source means computing a tighter upper bound (batas) on it, so the wording should make clear that SLC estimates the bound and does not reduce sensitivity. Two smaller points in [6]: "Introducing" is rendered as the imperative "Perkenalkan" where the announcement form "Memperkenalkan" is expected, and "beroverhed rendah" is a stiff loan calque.

examples.source: uses classical simulations to more tightly bound the sensitivity to errors throughout the circuit
examples.translation: menggunakan simulasi klasik untuk mengehadkan kepekaan terhadap ralat di seluruh Circuit dengan lebih ketat
examples.suggested: menggunakan simulasi klasik untuk menetapkan batas yang lebih ketat bagi kepekaan terhadap ralat di seluruh litar
examples.why: 'mengehadkan' reads as limiting/reducing sensitivity, but the addon tightens the estimated bound on it.

examples.source: Introducing Qiskit Paulice: a new addon

examples.suggested: pengesanan ralat kuantum dengan overhed rendah
examples.why: The 'ber-' prefix on the loanword 'overhed' is a stiff calque. A phrase with 'dengan' reads more naturally.

editor_note: The translation is faithful, and nothing in it would mislead a learner. A few spots need small fixes. "Deploy" is rendered as "digunakan/menggunakan" in [30], which reads as "use" and hides the deployment sense. "Pipeline" appears as "paip modular" in [30] but as "saluran paip (pipeline)" in [18]. In [35], "under similar conditions" became "keadaan yang sama" ("the same conditions"), which slightly overstates the claim, and "prestasi sejarah" is a calque. Core terms are rendered correctly and consistently: litar, boleh cerap, transpilasi, mitigasi ralat, and function/backend kept in English.

examples.source: All function templates are also readily deployable to Qiskit Serverless ... You can deploy your serverless package
examples.translation: Semua templat function juga sedia digunakan pada [Qiskit Serverless] ... Anda boleh menggunakan pakej serverless anda
examples.suggested: Semua templat function juga sedia untuk di-deploy / dikerahkan ke Qiskit Serverless ... Anda boleh mengerahkan (deploy) pakej serverless anda
examples.why: 'Digunakan/menggunakan' reads as 'used/use', so the sense of deployment is lost. Entry [30] also uses 'paip modular' for pipeline, while [18] uses 'saluran paip'.

examples.source: evaluate historical performance of an investment strategy and to enable comparisons of different portfolios under similar conditions
examples.translation: menilai prestasi sejarah strategi pelaburan dan membolehkan perbandingan portfolio berbeza di bawah keadaan yang sama
examples.suggested: menilai prestasi lampau strategi pelaburan dan membolehkan perbandingan portfolio berbeza di bawah keadaan yang serupa
examples.why: 'Sama' means identical, which is stronger than 'similar'. 'Prestasi sejarah' is a calque of 'historical performance'.

examples.source: Look up a single backend and confirm access with `backend()`.
examples.translation: Cari satu backend tunggal dan sahkan akses dengan `backend()`.
examples.suggested: Cari satu backend dan sahkan akses dengan `backend()`.
examples.why: 'Satu ... tunggal' is redundant and calques 'a single'.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful across all five entries. Entry [5] reads naturally ("telah dikeluarkan, untuk memigrasikan kod `qiskit-ibm-runtime`"), and the release date is correct. The one issue is "Qiskit skills". It is a named product: agent skills published in the Qiskit/skills repo, and entry [5] calls `migrate-qiskit-ibm-runtime` one of them. The file translates it every time as "kemahiran Qiskit" (entries [0], [1], [3], [5]). In a heading, that reads as "Qiskit proficiency", so a reader could think the page is about human skill with Qiskit rather than a set of tools. Keeping "skills" as a proper noun, e.g. "Qiskit skills" or "skill Qiskit", would be clearer. It is used consistently and does not change any factual claim, so this is minor.

examples.why: 'Qiskit skills' is a product name for agent skills from the Qiskit/skills repo. 'Kemahiran' means human proficiency, so the heading reads as 'Qiskit proficiency' instead of naming the tool collection.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout, and nothing would mislead a learner. The hedges in [9] survive: "might be faster" is kept as "mungkin lebih pantas" and "Perhaps most importantly" as "Mungkin yang paling penting". Two wording points remain. In [9], "menyediakan pengguna dengan keupayaan" copies the English "provide users with" word for word; Malay would say "menyediakan keupayaan ... kepada pengguna". Also, "release notes" is rendered as "nota pelancaran" (pelancaran means "launch") in [5] and [6], where software Malay usually says "nota keluaran".

examples.source: to provide users with the latest transpilation capabilities from the Qiskit SDK
examples.translation: untuk menyediakan pengguna dengan keupayaan transpilasi terkini daripada Qiskit SDK
examples.suggested: untuk menyediakan keupayaan transpilasi terkini daripada Qiskit SDK kepada pengguna
examples.why: 'menyediakan X dengan Y' copies the English 'provide X with Y' word for word. Standard Malay puts the thing provided first and the recipient after 'kepada'.
'Pelancaran' means launch. 'Nota keluaran' is the usual Malay term for software release notes. The current choice is still recognizable, so this is minor.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. A native editor would still fix some stiff phrasing. In [9], "Upgrades and ... enhancements" becomes "Peningkatan dan peningkatan prestasi", so the same word appears twice in a row. In [6], "Membina atas momentum yang ditetapkan" is a literal calque, and "ditetapkan" means "fixed/set", not "established". Across [0], [13] and [15], "release" is rendered as "pelancaran" ("launch"), while Malay software writing usually uses "keluaran" (e.g. "nota keluaran").

examples.source: Upgrades and Rust-driven performance enhancements to `VF2Layout` and `VF2PostLayout`
examples.translation: Peningkatan dan peningkatan prestasi didorong Rust kepada `VF2Layout` dan `VF2PostLayout`
examples.suggested: Naik taraf dan peningkatan prestasi berasaskan Rust pada `VF2Layout` dan `VF2PostLayout`
examples.why: The repeated 'peningkatan' reads like machine translation and blurs the difference between 'upgrades' and 'enhancements'.

examples.source: Building on the momentum established across the v2.x series
examples.translation: Membina atas momentum yang ditetapkan sepanjang siri v2.x
examples.suggested: Meneruskan momentum yang dibina sepanjang siri v2.x
examples.why: This is a calque of 'building on', and 'ditetapkan' means 'fixed/set', not 'established'.
'Pelancaran' means a product launch. Malay software writing more commonly uses 'keluaran' for a software release.

editor_note: I found no meaning drift. Dates, quantities (such as 250 µs to 4 ms, 68 ns versus 138 ns, and 20-500 µs to 20-2000 µs) and caveats all carry over correctly. The problem is terminology that shifts between the newer and older sections of the changelog. 'retire' is rendered as both 'dipersarakan' ([92]-[107]) and 'dinyahtauliahkan' ([148], [175], [223]). 'Open Plan' appears both kept in English and as 'Pelan Terbuka' ([151], [203]). 'instance' is both 'instans' and 'instance', 'Compute resources' is both kept in English and 'Sumber pengkomputeran', 'noise' is both 'bunyi bising' ([129]) and 'hingar' ([280]), and 'engine stack' is both 'timbunan' and 'tindanan'. There are also some calques and coinages ('menolak daya pemprosesan', 'menyunset', 'tarikh sunset'), and accordion titles are left in English in some places ('Third Quarter', 'Second quarter', 'First quarter') while others read 'Suku keempat' and 'Suku kedua'.

examples.source: The quantum computer `ibm_brisbane` has been retired
examples.why: [95] and [98] use 'dipersarakan' for the same event type, so retirement is rendered two ways in one file.

examples.source: to apply Pauli-twirling and to inject noise
examples.translation: menggunakan Pauli-twirling dan menyuntik bunyi bising
examples.why: 'bunyi bising' means acoustic noise. 'hingar' is the conventional technical term, and the file itself uses it in [280].

examples.source: welcomes `ibm_fez` and `ibm_marrakesh` to the Open Plan!
examples.why: The plan name is kept as 'Open Plan' in [65], [74] and [76] but becomes 'Pelan Terbuka' here and in [203], so the same product has two names.

examples.source: which pushes throughput above 100,000 Max Circuits Per Second (MCPS)
examples.translation: yang menolak daya pemprosesan melebihi 100,000 Litar Maksimum Sesaat (MCPS)
examples.suggested: sehingga daya pemprosesan melepasi 100,000 Litar Maksimum Sesaat (MCPS)
examples.why: 'menolak' is a literal calque of 'pushes' and reads unnaturally in Malay technical prose.

examples.source: We will eventually sunset IBM Quantum Platform classic
examples.translation: Kami akhirnya akan menyunset IBM Quantum Platform classic
examples.suggested: Kami akhirnya akan menamatkan IBM Quantum Platform Classic
examples.why: 'menyunset' is an ad-hoc coinage (and [233] has 'tarikh sunset'). Standard Malay has 'menamatkan' / 'tarikh penamatan'.

editor_note: Faithful and natural throughout, with no drift in the beta caveat or version requirement ("kini dalam beta dan memerlukan qiskit-ibm-runtime versi 0.47.0 atau lebih tinggi"), and consistent terms (noise→hingar, error mitigation→mitigasi ralat, directed execution model→model pelaksanaan terarah).
